newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-De La Rue H1 seen sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-De La Rue H1 seen sharply lower.

text.p: British printing and security products group De La Rue Plc was expected to post sharply lower first-half profits next week as analysts eagerly awaited news about the firm's strategy.
Analysts expected the company on Tuesday to report pretax profits of 55 to 61 million stg for the half year ended September 30 compared to 69.1 million stg a year ago.

"Something in the order of 15 to 20 percent (lower profits) is on the cards. But I think people are looking beyond these numbers to see the whole future of the group and the strategy," said Richard Finch, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, on Friday.
De La Rue warned in June that its first-half pretax profits would fall below last year, citing difficult trading conditions in its cash systems division and low banknote prices.

"The worst of the news appears to be over, but I think people are looking with this set of results to see where the forecasts will stabilise and whether we need to do another downgrade," said Panmure Gordon analyst Francesca Raleigh.
"As well as pricing pressure, (banknote) demand has fallen to a lower level. I think for the time being there's no reason why it shouldn't stay at the lower level," she added.
De La Rue's future profitability depends on its ability to develop its other businesses, including cash handling, outside its core banknote operations, analysts said.
"Banknote pricing is a very, very competitive market. All these companies are facing the challenge of finding other revenues -- and in the meantime you have an erosion of profits, said Finch.
De La Rue's shares dropped 8.5p to 549 in afternoon trade on Friday, continuing a weak trend ahead of the firm's results.
"I think the market is very nervous. They have had a habit of disappointing -- and surprising -- in the past," Finch said.
Difficulties in analysing the company's businesses contributed to market jitters.
"It's hard to quantify their businesses because they're either a greenfield investment or there's a security aspect, so they can't tell us about a contract," Finch said.
De La Rue was expected to maintain its dividend or increase it slightly from the year-ago level of 7.25p.
"I think that's perhaps a sideshow," Finch said. "What investors are clearly looking for is a sense that the company has direction."
